clue.text: This is the last month to speak out for honour

parts.note: December, the year's last month, is abbreviated DEC
to orate is to speak out in a formal, declaiming way

explanation.surface: Someone announces that this month is their final chance to speak up for honour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'This is' only leads in; the last month of the year gives DEC, and declaiming gives ORATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To decorate someone is to honour them with a medal or award.

clue.text: The guard put off accepting a tip

indicators.note: accepting means taking in, so one word holds the other

parts.note: to defer is to postpone or put off
an end is a tip, as the tip of a finger

explanation.surface: A security guard delays matters by taking a tip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'accepting' puts END inside DEFER.
explanation.definitionFit: A guard is one who protects, as does a protector or back in sport.

clue.text: Chapter on Italian's translated into Spanish

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means placed above, so the chapter letter comes first
translated means turned into another form, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters of Italian's, including the S

explanation.surface: A chapter in Italian has been translated into Spanish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'translated' rearranges ITALIANS to ASTILIAN, and C sits 'on' it in this down clue. The language of Castile is standard Spanish.
explanation.definitionFit: Castile's dialect is the standard form of the Spanish language.

clue.text: Sound agreement

parts.note: an agreement read as one that is in sound: words whose endings match in sound

explanation.definitionFit: Words whose endings correspond in sound, like cat and hat, agree in this way.

clue.text: Try to contain Oriental politician's violent outburst

indicators.note: to contain means one word holds the others within it

parts.note: a test is a trial or try
E, for east, is the oriental compass point
MP, member of parliament, is a politician

explanation.surface: An attempt to rein in an Eastern politician's tantrum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to contain' puts E and MP inside TEST. The held clue's 'lain' is an OCR stray; the page has no such word.
explanation.definitionFit: A storm is a violent outburst, and the word is used figuratively for an uproar.

clue.text: Mickey-taking cat?

parts.note: read literally, a cat that takes Mickey, the cartoon mouse, is a cat that catches mice; taking the mickey is British slang for teasing

explanation.surface: A cat that teases people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taking the mickey' is British slang for mocking someone; read literally, the cat takes Mickey Mouse, so it catches mice.
explanation.definitionFit: A cat kept or known for catching mice is called by this name.

clue.text: The order "Ride on" can be misinterpreted

indicators.note: be misinterpreted means the words are read wrongly, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An order to 'ride on' could be misunderstood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can' is fodder, not part of the signal; 'be misinterpreted' rearranges RIDE ON CAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A decree or regulation issued by authority is an official order.

clue.text: Strong drink

definitions.meaning: a dark beer such as porter

explanation.definitionFit: The word means sturdy or robust, and it is also a dark, heavy beer.

clue.text: Make a stand where one's accommodated by others

indicators.note: accommodated by means housed inside, so one piece is lodged in another

parts.note: the rest means the others
one's is read as one is, I plus IS

explanation.surface: Someone takes a stand where they are lodged with other people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one's' is read as 'one is', giving I'S; 'accommodated by' places it inside REST.
explanation.definitionFit: To oppose or withstand is to make a stand against something.

clue.text: Puts an end to waste in the Civil Service

indicators.note: in places the word for waste inside the abbreviation

parts.note: CS is the abbreviation for the Civil Service
to lose, as in time, is to waste it

explanation.surface: Someone ends wastefulness in the Civil Service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts LOSE inside CS. The Civil Service is Britain's body of government officials.
explanation.definitionFit: To end or finish something is to shut it down.

clue.text: Move back if pitch is dubious

indicators.note: move back tells us to turn the little word if round so it reads from the end

parts.note: taken as written before being turned
to pitch is to throw, and to shy is to throw a ball or stone

explanation.surface: A sports official warns that a dubious pitch may mean moving back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Move back' turns 'if' into FI; a 'shy' is a throw, as at a coconut shy.
explanation.definitionFit: Something suspicious or of doubtful honesty is described as smelling off in this way.

clue.text: "Divine _ truth," the nightingale sang

parts.note: fill the gap in Keats's line about the nightingale singing 'divine ... truth', from his poem 'Bards of Passion and of Mirth'; a tuneful word fits a songbird

explanation.walkthrough: The quotation is Keats: the nightingale sings 'not a senseless, tranced thing, but divine ... truth'; the missing word also describes birdsong.
explanation.definitionFit: The missing word means tuneful, which is what a nightingale's song is.

clue.text: Lionesses can be very quiet

indicators.note: can be suggests these letters could become something else when rearranged

explanation.surface: Big cats on the hunt are able to stay very quiet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can be' signals rearranging LIONESSES; the surface tempts you to read it as a fact about hunting lions.
explanation.definitionFit: Making no sound at all is being entirely silent, so very quiet.

clue.text: Determined to return the money

indicators.note: to return asks for the phrase for determined to be read from its end back to its start

parts.note: set on, as in 'set on winning', means determined

explanation.surface: Someone resolves to give the money back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to return' turns SET ON round; banknotes are 'the money'.
explanation.definitionFit: Banknotes are paper currency, so notes stands for money.

clue.text: Outstanding little gem in entire shop

indicators.note: little suggests only a small part of the run of words gem in entire is wanted

explanation.surface: A tiny jewel stands out in a shop full of them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'little' signals that the answer is a small part of 'gem in entire'; 'shop' is only part of the scene.
explanation.definitionFit: Distinguished or prominent people stand out from others, so they are notable.

clue.text: Crest seen displayed perhaps in raised position

indicators.note: displayed perhaps hints that the letters are set out in another way

explanation.surface: A crest is seen on show, perhaps in a raised position.
explanation.walkthrough: 'displayed perhaps' rearranges CREST SEEN.
explanation.definitionFit: The state of standing upright is a raised, vertical posture.

clue.text: Issue trap and lines

parts.note: issue means offspring, so a son
a net is a trap for fish or birds

explanation.surface: A list of three things: an issue, a trap and some lines.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Issue' means children, so SON; a poem is often called 'lines'.
explanation.definitionFit: A fourteen-line poem is a set of verse lines.

clue.text: One who is always interested in the outlook

definitions.text: One who is always interested in the outlook

parts.words: One who is always interested in the outlook
parts.note: outlook read as what lies outside oneself: a person whose attention is turned outward, to other people

explanation.definitionFit: An outgoing, sociable person focuses on the world outside the self.

clue.text: Fillet with pate set before the company

indicators.note: set before puts the head word in front of the company word

parts.note: a pate is the head
a band is a company or group

explanation.surface: A fillet with its head set out before the guests.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set before' puts HEAD in front of BAND. A fillet here is a ribbon worn round the head, not a cut of meat.
explanation.definitionFit: A fillet is a band worn round the hair or forehead.

clue.text: Popular action, certainly

parts.note: something popular is said to be in
a deed is an action

explanation.surface: Someone affirms that a popular measure will certainly go ahead.
explanation.definitionFit: Used as emphasis, the word means truly or without doubt.

clue.text: Put plainly, the river is without fish

indicators.note: without means outside, so the river is wrapped around the fish

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Britain
a cod is a fish

explanation.surface: To put it plainly, the river has no fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' means outside here, not lacking, so DEE goes round COD. The Dee is a river in Scotland and Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: To translate a coded message into ordinary language is to render it plainly.

clue.text: Showing uncommon respect for the royal staff

indicators.note: uncommon means unusual, so the letters of respect are put in an unusual order

explanation.surface: Palace servants are shown unusual deference.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Showing' is a link; 'uncommon' rearranges RESPECT. 'Royal staff' looks like palace employees but is the rod a monarch carries.
explanation.definitionFit: A monarch's ornamental rod, carried as a symbol of sovereignty, is a royal staff.

clue.text: Clean up for example as punishment

parts.note: to scour is to clean by scrubbing

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the short abbreviation is read from the bottom upward

explanation.surface: Being made to clean up, say, as a punishment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses EG to GE under SCOUR; 'Clean up' looks like one phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: A whip, and figuratively any affliction, is a means of punishment.

clue.text: Flat includes parking, which is essential

indicators.note: includes means one word takes in another

parts.note: stale beer is flat

explanation.surface: An advert insists that a flat with parking is essential.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flat' looks like an apartment but means stale; 'includes' puts P inside STALE.
explanation.definitionFit: A basic, principal item, as in staple foods, is an essential one.

clue.text: Quite impervious and decidedly mean

definitions.meaning: as in watertight or airtight, sealed so nothing passes
a stingy person is said to be close-fisted in this way

explanation.surface: Someone is described as both thick-skinned and stingy.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means sealed fast so nothing gets through, and also miserly with money.

clue.text: A coloured politician?

parts.note: a politician named after a colour: a member of the environmental party

explanation.definitionFit: A member of the environmental party takes its name from a colour.

clue.text: Expression of displeasure or distraction

definitions.meaning: an angry word, split into two words
a puzzle that diverts the mind, a pastime

explanation.surface: Grumbling, or something to take one's mind off things.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as two words it is an angry remark; as one it is the puzzle you are solving.
explanation.definitionFit: An angry remark is a harsh word spoken in temper; the puzzle in the newspaper is a pastime that diverts the mind.

clue.text: Pole with English husband

parts.note: a spar is a pole, as on a ship

explanation.surface: A Polish man with an English husband.
explanation.walkthrough: 'husband' is a verb meaning to use sparingly; 'Pole' is a rod, not a Polish man.
explanation.definitionFit: To husband resources is to economise with them, to save them.

clue.text: He claims to be soft, touching, and caring

parts.note: P, short for piano, is the musical abbreviation for soft
re means concerning or touching on
tender means caring or gentle

explanation.surface: A man insists he is gentle, moving and kind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'touching' means 'about', hence RE; the definition is a person who claims a throne or title.
explanation.definitionFit: A claimant to a throne or title is one who asserts a right to it.

clue.text: Lists taking an age to turn over

indicators.note: to turn over asks for the whole run of letters to be read backwards

parts.note: an era is an age or period

explanation.surface: Lists that take forever to be turned over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to turn over' reverses AN ERA. In old usage 'the lists' were the enclosed ground where knights jousted.
explanation.definitionFit: The lists were the enclosed field for a tournament, so a place for contests.

clue.text: Jack Worthing given a home by Her Majesty

indicators.note: by means beside, placing the Queen's letters next to the home

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the Queen
a nest is a home

explanation.surface: A man named Jack Worthing is taken in by the Queen.
explanation.walkthrough: In Wilde's play The Importance of Being Earnest, Jack Worthing calls himself by this name in town. ER = the Queen (Elizabeth Regina).
explanation.definitionFit: Wilde's character Jack Worthing uses this assumed first name in the play's London scenes.

clue.text: Disliked being flung into the long grass

indicators.note: into places the word for flung inside the word for the tall grass

parts.note: a reed is a tall grass growing by water
sent means thrown or flung

explanation.surface: Someone resented being thrown into tall grass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being flung' gives SENT; 'into' puts it inside REED.
explanation.definitionFit: To be aggrieved by something is to feel bitterness about it, to dislike it.
